title: Degree filtration bounds and compatible monoid truncations
statement:
Let $r\geq0$ be an integer, let $Q\subseteq\mathbf N^r$ be a finitely generated additive submonoid, and let $L$ be a commutative ring with ideal $\mathfrak a$. Write $B=L[Q]$ for the ring of finite sums $\sum_{q\in Q}c_qz^q$, with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$, and let $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Put $|e|=\sum_i e_i$, $J=\mathfrak aB+(z^q:q\in Q\setminus\{0\})$, $I=\mathfrak aA+(X_1,\ldots,X_r)A$, and define $j:B\to A$ by $j(\sum_qc_qz^q)=\sum_qc_qX^q$. Choose any finite list of nonzero additive generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$ and put $D=\max(\{1\}\cup\{|q_i|:1\leq i\leq s\})$; for $Q=\{0\}$ the list may be empty and $D=1$. Then $j$ is an injective $L$-algebra homomorphism, and for every $n\geq0$, with $E_n=j^{-1}(I^n)$, one has
$$J^n\subseteq E_n,\qquad E_{Dn}\subseteq J^n.$$
For every series $F=\sum_{q\in Q}c_qX^q$ whose coefficients outside $Q$ vanish, define the finite sum $b_n(F)=\sum_{q\in Q,\ |q|<Dn}c_qz^q\in B$. For all $m\geq n\geq0$,
$$b_m(F)-b_n(F)\in J^n,\qquad F-j(b_n(F))\in I^{Dn}.$$
Thus $(b_n(F)\bmod J^n)_n$ is an element of $\varprojlim_n B/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every $e\in\mathbf N^r$ and every $n$ with $Dn>|e|$, the $e$-coefficient of $j(b_n(F))$ equals the $e$-coefficient of $F$.

proof.text: The coefficient of $X^e$ in $j(b)$ is the $z^e$-coefficient of $b$ if $e\in Q$, and zero otherwise. Thus $j$ is injective. The finite convolution formula of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] gives $j(bb\prime)=j(b)j(b\prime)$; addition and constants are preserved coefficientwise. For $q\ne0$, some $q_i>0$, so $X^q=X_iX^{q-\epsilon_i}\in I$. Also $j(\mathfrak aB)\subseteq I$. Hence $j(J)\subseteq I$, and multiplying $n$ factors and adding gives $J^n\subseteq E_n$ (including $n=0$).

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), gives the motivating completed monoid models only. The following finite coefficient and generator-length argument is by Q41; the coefficient criterion is lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients.

proof.text: For $q\in Q$, choose $q=\sum_{i=1}^s k_iq_i$ and set $\ell=\sum_i k_i$. Then $z^q=\prod_i(z^{q_i})^{k_i}\in J^\ell$ and $|q|=\sum_i k_i|q_i|\leq D\ell$. Also $c\in\mathfrak a^t$ implies $cz^q\in J^{t+\ell}$: expand $c$ as a finite sum of products of $t$ elements of $\mathfrak a$ and multiply by the displayed monomial. These statements include $q=0$ with all $k_i=0$.

proof.text: Let $b=\sum_qc_qz^q\in E_{Dn}$. For each of its finitely many terms use $\ell$ from Step 2. If $\ell\geq n$, then $c_qz^q\in J^n$. Otherwise $|q|\leq D\ell<Dn$, and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients], with coefficient ideal $\mathfrak a$ and exponent $Dn$, gives $c_q\in\mathfrak a^{Dn-|q|}$. Since $Dn-|q|\geq D(n-\ell)\geq n-\ell$, Step 2 and decreasing ideal powers give $c_qz^q\in J^n$ again. Adding proves $E_{Dn}\subseteq J^n$. For $n=0$ every term is in the first case.

proof.text: The set of $e\in\mathbf N^r$ with $|e|<Dn$ is finite: when $Dn>0$ each coordinate is less than $Dn$, and when $Dn=0$ it is empty. Thus $b_n(F)$ is a finite sum. For $m\geq n$, $b_m(F)-b_n(F)$ is supported on $Dn\leq|q|<Dm$. Step 2 gives $D\ell\geq|q|\geq Dn$, hence $\ell\geq n$ since $D\geq1$. Every term belongs to $J^n$, proving the asserted difference congruence.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), gives the motivating completed monoid models only. The following finite coefficient and generator-length argument is by Q41; the coefficient criterion is lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients.

proof.text: Every coefficient of $F-j(b_n(F))$ of degree less than $Dn$ is zero, including exponents outside $Q$ by the support hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with ideal $\mathfrak a$ and exponent $Dn$; zero belongs to each required coefficient ideal, so $F-j(b_n(F))\in I^{Dn}$. The same coefficient description gives the asserted exact equality at every $e$ with $|e|<Dn$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), gives the motivating completed monoid models only. The following finite coefficient and generator-length argument is by Q41; the coefficient criterion is lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients.

proof.text: The transition $B/J^m\to B/J^n$ for $m\geq n$ sends the class of $b_m(F)$ to the class of $b_n(F)$ by Step 4. Thus these classes form a compatible sequence, which is precisely an element of the inverse limit in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. At level zero the quotient is $B/J^0=0$, so this also includes $n=0$.

lean.statement: theorem monoid_degree_filtration_truncations (L : Type u) [CommRing L] (r : ℕ) (Q : AddSubmonoid (Fin r →₀ ℕ)) (a : Ideal L) (s : ℕ) (q : Fin s → Q) (h_nonzero : ∀ i : Fin s, q i ≠ 0) (h_generates : AddSubmonoid.closure (Set.range q) = ⊤) : ∃ j : AddMonoidAlgebra L Q →ₐ[L] MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L, (∀ f : AddMonoidAlgebra L Q, j f = f.coeff.sum (fun e c ↦ MvPowerSeries.monomial (e : Fin r →₀ ℕ) c)) ∧ Function.Injective j ∧ ∃ (J : Ideal (AddMonoidAlgebra L Q)) (I : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L)) (D : ℕ), J = Ideal.map (algebraMap L (AddMonoidAlgebra L Q)) a ⊔ Ideal.span {x | ∃ e : Q, e ≠ 0 ∧ x = AddMonoidAlgebra.single e (1 : L)} ∧ I = Ideal.map (algebraMap L (MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L)) a ⊔ Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin r → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L)) ∧ D = max 1 ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin s)).sup (fun i ↦ (q i : Fin r →₀ ℕ).degree)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, J ^ n ≤ Ideal.comap j.toRingHom (I ^ n) ∧ Ideal.comap j.toRingHom (I ^ (D * n)) ≤ J ^ n) ∧ ∀ F : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L, (∀ e : Fin r →₀ ℕ, e ∉ Q → MvPowerSeries.coeff e F = 0) → ∃ b : ℕ → AddMonoidAlgebra L Q, (∀ n : ℕ, b n = ∑ e ∈ (Finsupp.finite_of_degree_lt (σ := Fin r) (D * n)).toFinset, if h : e ∈ Q then AddMonoidAlgebra.single ⟨e, h⟩ (MvPowerSeries.coeff e F) else 0) ∧ (∀ m n : ℕ, n ≤ m → b m - b n ∈ J ^ n ∧ F - j (b n) ∈ I ^ (D * n)) ∧ (∃ x : AdicCompletion J (AddMonoidAlgebra L Q), ∀ n : ℕ, AdicCompletion.evalₐ J n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ n) (b n)) ∧ ∀ (e : Fin r →₀ ℕ) (n : ℕ), e.degree < D * n → MvPowerSeries.coeff e (j (b n)) = MvPowerSeries.coeff e F
